newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares close down on interest rate fears.
newsitem.headline: French shares close down on interest rate fears.

text.p: French shares fell on Monday in line with other share markets on fears that the U.S. Federal Reserve may decide to raise interest rates at the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday.
Brokers said the bourse's fall also reflected profit-taking on the last day of the September account, which ended with a 2.29 percent gain.
The market has risen 10.42 percent so far this year.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 12.37 points, or 0.59 percent, at 2,067.09 on Monday, while the CAC-40 September futures contract fell 10.5 points to 2,072.
Volume was a modest 3.05 billion francs.
Most analysts expect the Fed to raise its Fed funds rate by a quarter point on Tuesday.
"If the Fed raises rates by 25 basis points then you can say it is already priced in, but if it raises them by 50 points, then prices will fall," a dealer said.

Many investors were sidelined ahead of the FOMC meeting as well as a series of important corporate results due this week, including those of Alcatel Alsthom, LVMH, Lafarge, Canal Plus and insurer Axa.
Carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen closed down 2.4 percent at 569 francs after reporting its first half profit shrank by half as carmakers waged a price war in the French car market.
